transaction_plan: Verify frozen baseline/candidate bytes, exact allowed transformation, plan, independent candidate-byte judgment, current schema and exporter checks.
Acquire an exclusive advisory package lock; reject symlink targets, unknown byte states, and changed pinned inputs. This coordinates cooperating writers only.
Persist an intent receipt with before/candidate/judgment/preflight bindings before writing canonical data.
Stage approved candidate bytes on the same filesystem; fsync, recheck the target against expected baseline immediately before atomic os.replace, then fsync the containing directory.
Run the real complete Numbers export against actual current canonical file; require target text/note match candidate and all other exported content match baseline overlay.
Reproduce frozen sample with only the baseline-byte overlay; verify all101 context bindings, separately record current corpus change. Unknown third target states and unrelated drift fail.

Persist final application receipt with exact resulting bytes and validation results. Never reuse an old receipt for different content; if interrupted at approved candidate state, resume only from matching intent.
A post-swap validation failure remains a recorded failed/incomplete transaction, not publication approval; do not overwrite an intervening user edit during recovery.
atomicity_limit: Atomic replacement makes canonical file visibility all-or-nothing, but intent/final ledger and target are not a multi-file atomic transaction. A cooperating advisory lock and immediate expected-byte check do not exclude a noncooperating writer in the final check-to-replace interval; no claim of general compare-and-swap is made.
